appearance.organs.*.inflorescence.spathe.why: An aroid's spathe is drawn as long, against its spadix, as the flora gives the two.

traits.perianth.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213: perianth of 2+2 or 3+3 (rarely 4+4) tepals, or absent (Floral Diagrams p. 96: none or 6).

traits.flower_merosity.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213: tepals in whorls of 2 or 3.

traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213: stamens 4, 6 or 8, rarely 1 to 12.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213: ovary of 3, rarely 1 to about 50, carpels.

traits.ovary_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213: flowers hypogynous with a superior ovary.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213: Simpson states the hypanthium is absent.

traits.leaf_division.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Araceae: leaves simple or compound; the blade's dissection is not coded. The rest is inferred from the genera: most blades are simple and entire (Lysichiton, Calla, Peltandra, Arum, Zantedeschia, Anthurium, Colocasia, Spathiphyllum), some are pinnately lobed or cut (Philodendron, Monstera), and the compound ones are palmate or pedate (Arisaema, Syngonium) or much divided (Amorphophallus, Dracunculus).

traits.leaf_incision.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Araceae: leaves simple or compound; the blade's dissection is not coded. rules.note: What the cluster's `spathe` means: the spathe's length as a share of its spadix's axis, a spathe's sheath included.

traits.note: Abrams's flora (vol. 1, 1923): the arum family's flowers are small and crowded on a spadix, which a spathe encloses or stands below; the perianth is of four to six scale-like parts or lacking.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Araceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Acoraceae, Lemnaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded often a basal rosette, often no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Araceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Acoraceae, Lemnaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded usually perennial, sometimes annual. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213, 214, 215, family Araceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral (or distichous), usually; read as {"spiral": "usually"}.

traits.bract_form.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213, 214, 215, family Araceae: bract form spathe (prominent, often coloured), usually; read as {"spathe": "usually"}.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213, 214, 215, family Araceae: flower symmetry actinomorphic; read as "actinomorphic".

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213, 214, 215, family Araceae: sexual system monoecious (female flowers proximal, male distal), often; read as {"monoecious": "often"}.

traits.fruit_type.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213, 214, 215, family Araceae: fruit type multiple (of berries; sometimes dry utricles), usually; read as {"multiple": "usually"}.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 213, 214, 215, family Araceae: rhizome habit short_creeping (rhizomes, corms, tubers or reduced), often; read as {"short_creeping": "often"}.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Araceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded often a corm, often a rhizome, often tubers. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.
